speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant has been having recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing; could you describe exactly when these episodes occur and what triggers them? How old is the infant, and have you noticed any specific activities, such as feeding or crying, that seem to worsen the symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the stridor and respiratory distress improve when the infant's neck is extended or when he is lying prone? I also need to know if there is a history of choking or cyanosis during these episodes.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of stridor that worsens with neck flexion and improves with extension is highly suggestive of vascular compression, specifically vascular ring syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Barium swallow study

speaker: Doctor
text: It is unusual for the CT angiography to be normal given the barium swallow findings, so I need to rule out other causes like laryngomalacia or subglottic stenosis. REQUEST TEST: Flexible Laryngoscopy and Bronchoscopy

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal laryngoscopy and CT angiography are puzzling given the classic clinical presentation of neck-flexion induced stridor. I will request images to see if there are subtle anatomical clues missed by the text reports. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic symptoms of stridor worsening with neck flexion and feeding, along with the barium swallow findings, I am confident in the diagnosis despite the normal CT. DIAGNOSIS READY: Vascular Ring Syndrome
